title: She remembered (Sotah 13a)
hookLine: Serach daughter of Asher lived long enough to show Moses where Joseph's coffin lay
tomorrow: Pharaoh's decree comes down. her parents give up. why doesn't she?

lines: THE ONE WHO KNOWS WHERE THINGS ARE.
cards: A family often has one person who knows where things are: the spare key, the important papers, which cousin can't eat nuts. Nobody notices that job until the day it matters.
In the Talmud, the Israelites are finally leaving Egypt, and Moses has an old promise to keep, and no idea where to find it.

teach.b: Joseph had made his family swear to carry his bones out of Egypt. The Torah says: "And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him." But where were they?
The Talmud says one person from that old generation was still alive: Serach, daughter of Asher, Joseph's niece. She remembered.
The Egyptians, she told him, had sealed Joseph in a metal coffin and sunk it in the Nile. Moses went to the bank and called out to Joseph, and the coffin rose.

One to tell a friend tonight: in this telling, the whole exodus waits on one woman's memory. Serach is named in a family list in Genesis and almost nowhere else in the Torah, yet the rabbis gave her this moment.
She isn't the leader or the prophet.
She's the one who remembered, so the others could carry it.
Set her beside this week's other voices: Rachel, Rabban Yochanan, Nachshon. Each held something for the people who came after. Serach held a place.

how: Jewish families keep memory through names, stories at the Shabbat and seder table, and yahrzeit candles lit each year for loved ones who have died.

o: Serach recalled where Joseph's coffin lay
Miriam hid the baby Moses in the river reeds
Rachel kept her father's idols in a saddle

games.q: who kept the memory — tap the pairs.
p: made his family swear to carry his bones
calls out at the bank, and it rises

s: in the Talmud, Moses already knew where Joseph was buried
he had to ask Serach, daughter of Asher, the one who remembered.
Serach is named in the Torah itself
she appears in a family list in Genesis; the rabbis gave her this moment.

games.q: your grandmother is the only one who knows how her soup is made, and it's never been written down. by Serach's story, what matters most?
o: someone sits with her soon and learns it, so it can be carried on.
wait for a holiday, when it's her turn to make it anyway.
find a close recipe online; the small details don't really matter.
games.why: in the Talmud, the exodus waited on one person's memory. the one who remembers is how the rest get to carry it.

practice: Choose one memory of your family or friends that could get lost: a recipe, a saying, how two people met, the name of an old street. Say it out loud, slowly, as if to someone who will need it later.
If someone is near, tell them; if not, say it to the room, and let it be kept.

wordCard.voice: She remembered: Serach, daughter of Asher, who in the Talmud knew where Joseph's coffin lay, when no one else did.

orig.note: Hebrew name: Serach, daughter of Asher, named in Genesis 46:17.

carryVoice: Hold this one: she remembered, and so the whole people could carry Joseph home. That's the week, thirty-six days into the block.

sources.ref: Babylonian Talmud, Sotah 13a (Moses asks Serach daughter of Asher; the metal coffin sunk in the Nile; Moses calls and it rises)
